title: Greek Philosophy: From the Presocratics to Aristotle

questions.question: Thales, traditionally the first Greek philosopher, held that the arche (first principle) of all things is:
questions.rationale: Thales of Miletus (c. 624–546 BCE) proposed water as the single underlying nature of things — the first logos-style explanation.

questions.question: Which pair of Presocratics set philosophy's central metaphysical agenda — the changeless One versus universal flux?
questions.rationale: Parmenides argued that change is an illusion of the senses, while Heraclitus taught that everything flows like fire — permanence versus flux.

questions.question: Democritus explained the world as:
options: Four elements plus a cosmic mind
Indivisible atoms moving in the void
questions.rationale: Democritus' atomism posited changeless particles whose changing arrangements produce the world — a reply to both Parmenides and Heraclitus.

questions.question: 'Man is the measure of all things' expresses which movement's relativism?
options: The Sophists, as taught by Protagoras
questions.rationale: Protagoras, a Sophist, made truth relative to the perceiver; the Sophists were travelling paid teachers whom Plato distrusted.

questions.question: Socrates' characteristic method of cross-examining a claim until it yields agreement or contradiction is called:
questions.rationale: The elenchus tests claims by drawing out their consequences; Socrates wrote nothing — we know him through Plato, Xenophon, and Aristophanes.

questions.question: In Plato's allegory of the cave, the sun outside stands for:
questions.rationale: The escaped prisoner finally sees the sun — the Form of the Good, source of truth and being for all other Forms.

questions.question: Plato's Republic grounds the ideal state on which psychology?
options: The soul is a harmony of the four humours
The soul has three parts — reason, spirit, appetite
The soul is a stream of perceptions
questions.rationale: Reason should rule with spirit as ally and appetite obedient: philosopher-kings, guardians, and producers each do their own work — that is justice.

questions.question: A sculptor's labour is to a statue as the ______ cause is to it:
questions.rationale: Aristotle's four causes: bronze (material), the design (formal), the sculptor's work (efficient), and the purpose of honouring a god (final).

questions.question: Unlike Plato, Aristotle holds that:
options: Forms exist in a separate realm
Forms exist within things, and knowledge begins with the senses
questions.rationale: Aristotle's empiricism keeps forms immanent in substances; against Plato's separate, recollected Forms.

questions.question: Which Hellenistic school sought apatheia — freedom from destructive passions — through reason?
questions.rationale: Zeno of Citium's Stoicism taught living by reason and controlling only what is up to us — later embodied by Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius.
